/-!
# Erdős Problem 109

*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/109](https://www.erdosproblems.com/109)
- [MRR19] J. Moreira, F.K. Richter, and D. Robertson, A proof of a sumset conjecture of Erdős,
  Annals of Math. 189 (2019), 605-652.
-/

@[expose] public section

open Pointwise

namespace Erdos109

/--
Any $A\subseteq \mathbb{N}$ of positive upper density contains a sumset $B+C$ where both $B$ and $C$
are infinite.

The Erdős sumset conjecture. Proved by Moreira, Richter, and Robertson [MRR19].
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5, formal_proof using lean4 at
  "https://github.com/plby/lean-proofs/blob/8822f7ddef30fadbd92e1c6ab4ed897af356af5e/src/latest/ErdosProblems/Erdos109.lean#L9074"]
theorem erdos_109 (A : Set ℕ) (h : A.upperDensity > 0) :
    ∃ B C : Set ℕ, B.Infinite ∧ C.Infinite ∧ B + C ⊆ A := by
  sorry

end Erdos109

reformulations.difference: Set.upperDensity uses |A ∩ {0,…,n−1}|/n, whereas the cited paper defines upper density using |A ∩ {1,…,n}|/n.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: For n > 0, the two numerators differ by the indicator of 0 ∈ A minus the indicator of n ∈ A, so the ratios differ in absolute value by at most 1/n. Consequently their limsups coincide. If ℕ in the source is understood to exclude zero, removing zero from A does not change its upper density; zero can also be removed from both infinite summand sets without destroying infinitude or sumset containment. The scratch file proves this last witness-removal equivalence.

review.notes: The sole theorem faithfully states the conjecture in §1 of the cited paper, and its research solved tag agrees with the paper's affirmative solution. Lean checks in /workspace/review/scratch.lean verified the density formula, its finite cardinality and boundedness conditions, zero-prefix behavior, density zero for finite sets, density one for ℕ, density one-half for the evens, and ordinary pointwise-sum semantics. The cited external proof was compiled in /workspace/review/ExternalProofCheck.lean after replacing its Util.Density import with Mathlib and the repository's matching density definitions. Its axiom report was exactly [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]. The Erdős Problems URL returned a Cloudflare 403 despite descriptive User-Agent headers; statement verification therefore used the directly cited primary paper.
